body.title: fix(release): refuse a null entry in --assets-links
body.description:
## Description

When the JSON array given to `--assets-links` contained `null`, `glab release create` and `glab release upload` decoded it to a nil `*upload.ReleaseAsset` and later dereferenced it, so glab panicked with a nil pointer dereference and exit status 2. By then it could already have changed the release: `upload` added the links that came before the `null` one, and `create` updated an existing release and added them too. v1.124.0 also creates a new release and its first links before it panics; on `main`, since !4040, a new release panics before the release is created.

This MR moves the decoding of `--assets-links` into one helper, `releaseutils.AssetLinksFromJSON`, next to `releaseutils.AssetsFromArgs`, and calls it from both commands where they decoded the flag before. It refuses a `null` element with `failed to parse JSON string: the asset link at index <n> is null`, counting from 0, and keeps the error for malformed JSON as it was. Both commands parse the flag before their first request (create in `complete`, upload in `validate`), so the command now fails without touching the release.

I chose to refuse a `null` element rather than skip it, since it can only be a mistake in the input and malformed input is refused already. Tell me if you would rather skip it.

## Related Issues

Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/8684

## How has this been tested?

I added `TestReleaseCreate_InvalidAssetsLinksJSON` and `TestReleaseUpload_InvalidAssetsLinksJSON`, one in each command, each with three cases: `[null]`, a valid link followed by `null`, and malformed JSON. They set no mock expectations, so a request of any kind fails them. On `main` at a6fd50cecb4bbe630dfb03a621cbe2cedfef4aef the two `null` cases fail in both tests, because the commands go on to call `GetTag` and `GetRelease`, and the malformed JSON case passes. With the change all six cases pass, and so do the existing `--assets-links` tests of both commands.

With Go 1.27.3 and golangci-lint 2.14.0 on this branch: `make test-race` passes (6726 tests, 18 skipped), `make lint` reports 0 issues, `golangci-lint fmt --diff` is empty, `go run ./scripts/comment-overlap -threshold 1.0 -max-findings 0 ./cmd/... ./internal/...` reports 0 findings, `make check-embed check-args` is clean, and `make gen-docs` and `make generate` change no file. The commit message and the title pass commitlint with `scripts/commit-lint/.commitlintrc.js`.

Each of these changes to the code makes at least one of the new cases fail: removing the `null` check, inverting it, skipping `null` elements instead of refusing them, reporting the index plus one, and going back to `json.Unmarshal` in either command alone.

End to end, I built glab from v1.124.0, from `main` and from this branch, and ran the three commands of the issue against a small local HTTP server that answers the tag and release endpoints the way GitLab does and logs each request:

| Command | v1.124.0 | `main` | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `release create`, new release | panic, exit status 2, after creating the release and link `a` | panic, exit status 2, after GET tag and GET release | error, exit status 1, no request |
| `release create`, existing release | panic, exit status 2, after updating the release and adding link `b` | as v1.124.0 | error, exit status 1, no request |
| `release upload` | panic, exit status 2, after adding link `c` | as v1.124.0 | error, exit status 1, no request |

On this branch each of the three prints `failed to parse JSON string: the asset link at index 1 is null.` and exits with status 1.

This comes from maintaining [gitlab-mcp-server](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server); its [upstream-bugs.md](https://github.com/jmrplens/gitlab-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/development/upstream-bugs.md) records everything done on its dependencies and sibling projects.
